scenes.headline: Python Syntax & Basics
scenes.subtitle: The rules that shape every line of Python you write
scenes.narration: Before you build pipelines, it helps to know the handful of syntax rules that shape every line of Python.

scenes.headline: The core rules
items: The hash symbol starts a comment
One statement per line, no semicolons
scenes.narration: In Python, indentation is not just style; it defines which lines belong to a block, so consistent spacing is essential. You never declare a variable's type because Python infers it from the value you assign. A hash symbol turns the rest of a line into a comment that the interpreter ignores. And each statement lives on its own line, so you rarely need semicolons at all.

scenes.headline: Variables and printing
scenes.code:
name = "pipeline"
retries = 3
active = True

print(f"{name} running, retries={retries}")
scenes.narration: Here we assign a string, a number, and a boolean without ever stating their types. Python figures out each type from the value on the right. The final line uses an f-string to print those variables inside a readable message, which is the everyday way to combine text and data.

scenes.headline: Indentation is meaningful
scenes.narration: On the left, the indented line clearly belongs to the if statement, and four spaces per level is the accepted convention. On the right, the missing indentation breaks that relationship and Python raises an IndentationError. Getting spacing right is the difference between code that runs and code that refuses to start.

scenes.headline: How Python runs your file
scenes.narration: You write your code in a plain text file ending in dot py. The interpreter reads it from top to bottom and runs each statement in order. As it goes, it either produces output or stops at the first error it cannot resolve.

scenes.text: Whitespace is syntax in Python, so keep your indentation clean and consistent.
scenes.narration: The key habit to carry forward is treating whitespace as real syntax, so keep your indentation clean and consistent from the start.
